title: 1 Relatively Safe and Undervalued Dividend Stock to Buy Right Now in November
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc makes the case for PepsiCo as a relatively safe, undervalued stock to buy in November, stressing that relatively safe does not mean risk-free, only that it avoids the fast-moving technology risks of AI and software names. Wall Street forecasts about 5.5% earnings-per-share growth a year, but he estimates 7-9%, driven by low-to-mid single-digit revenue growth with costs under control creating operating leverage. The cheap valuation reflects a decade of underperformance against Coca-Cola on profitability: Coke's operating margin is over 32% against PepsiCo's 15.8%, and Coke's margins have improved from 22% to 32% over the decade while PepsiCo's have sat near 16%. He sees that gap as room to improve, especially if PepsiCo adopts Coke-like bottler and distributor practices that investors are pushing for. PepsiCo also carries a return on invested capital of about 15%, above its cost of capital, and a forward P/E of 16.6 against Coke's 27.5. Call: PEP BUY at ~$143, DCF fair value $190, BUY reiterated from 12 October. No flip. Bull: margin gains close the Coca-Cola gap and re-rate the stock. Bear: the shift to healthier options pressures sugary drinks and snacks. Coca-Cola (KO) is the only other ticker discussed, as the comparison case.
